items.title: Beyond the Agent
items.tagline: Make persistent intelligence falsifiable instead of treating every new paradigm as a feature.
items.problem: The frontier-reset research changes the question from: How do we make an agent reason, remember, route, and act better? to: Why should cognition be organized as repeated agent episodes at all? items.title: Differential Mind
items.tagline: Update only reasoning consequences affected by a relevant world delta.
items.problem: Hermes should investigate whether cognition can become a maintained incremental computation rather than a sequence of fresh reasoning episodes. The key distinction is stronger than caching: when inputs change, only affected cognitive consequences should update. Long-run hypothesis: cognitive work scales with the causally relevant world delta, not accumulated history.
items.outcome: A strict comparison of differential update versus caching and full recompute. Proposed discriminator: In recurring environments with sparse changes, maintained cognitive dependencies preserve verified outcomes while recomputing asymptotically less semantic work than episode-based Hermes.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
What are the stable nodes/dependencies of a persistent cognitive computation?
Which reasoning operations admit lawful deltas?

items.title: Quotient Mind
items.tagline: Merge histories only when no relevant future action can distinguish them.
items.problem: Hermes should investigate whether true cognitive state should be defined by behavioral distinguishability rather than textual completeness. Two histories are the same state when no relevant future experiment/action can distinguish them in a way that changes attainable outcomes or policy. This is not "compress the transcript better." It quotients history space itself.
items.outcome: Test behaviorally sufficient state against exact recall and safety counterexamples. Proposed discriminator: Across recurring environments, decision-distinct states grow substantially slower than raw histories while preserving verified outcomes.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
Does software/personal-assistant life admit a compact behavioral quotient?
Relative to which futures is equivalence defined?

items.title: Assumption-Lattice Mind
items.tagline: Retain incompatible possible worlds instead of silently choosing one story.
items.problem: Hermes should investigate epistemic non-commitment as a core architecture. Instead of forcing contradictory or uncertain evidence into one fluent state, maintain explicit assumptions, consequences derived under assumption sets, incompatible possible worlds, nogoods/contradictions, actions valid across worlds, and discriminating observations only when the difference matters.
items.outcome: Find safe world-invariant actions and low-cost discriminating observations. Proposed discriminator: For contradictory, stale and partially observed work, preserving alternative worlds reduces false commitment and repeated re-reasoning without prohibitive combinatorial growth.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
How often can Hermes act correctly without resolving which world is true?
When should uncertainty be probability versus discrete incompatible worlds?

items.title: Sheaf Mind
items.tagline: Preserve domain-native local representations without privileging one global schema.
items.problem: Hermes should investigate an architecture with no universal cognitive state or ontology. Code, UI, user preferences, security, tools, visual perception, calendars and repositories may each retain their natural representations. Coordination occurs through overlap/translation maps. Global coherence exists only when compatible local views can be glued; incompatibility becomes an explicit obstruction.
items.outcome: Verify overlap compatibility and explain irreconcilable local views. Proposed discriminator: For sufficiently heterogeneous tasks, local-native representations plus explicit overlap consistency preserve more useful structure with less translation than a universal global state.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
Which Hermes domains genuinely need a common representation?
What information belongs only on overlaps?

items.title: Viability Mind
items.tagline: Treat future human options, reversibility and controllability as first-class objectives.
items.problem: Hermes should investigate whether the persistent objective of a personal intelligence should be preservation and expansion of viable future agency rather than completion of the current inferred task. A viability-oriented intelligence asks which actions make progress while preserving recoverability, reversibility, observability, human choice, authority and useful future options.
items.outcome: Compare task-only rewards with independent viability measures. Proposed discriminator: For ambiguous, long-horizon or irreversible work, policies that explicitly preserve viable future options reduce unrecoverable failures without unacceptable task paralysis.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
What constitutes future agency in digital/personal work?
Can reversibility, authority, information access, human choice and recovery live in one formal object?

items.title: Event-Triggered Cognition
items.tagline: Buy additional thinking and observation only when expected decision value justifies it.

items.title: Causal Scale & Predictive State
items.tagline: Choose file, task or project abstraction where decision-relevant cause lives.
items.problem: At what causal scale should Hermes represent a problem? Current systems usually choose scale architecturally: token, message, file, tool call, task, project, agent. This issue asks whether scale itself should be a learned/dynamic property chosen according to where causal information lives.
items.outcome: Detect when coarse state is insufficient and refine without lost provenance.
journeys: A researcher pins an old-world comparator and a frozen test environment, with no live Hermes authority.
Can causal contribution identify when file-level reasoning beats line-level reasoning, or project-level reasoning beats file-level reasoning?

items.title: Equivalence-Saturated Deliberation
items.tagline: Retain proven equivalent action plans to avoid redundant replanning.
items.problem: Can Hermes avoid repeated planning by representing equivalence among actions/plans rather than repeatedly selecting and revising one trajectory?
items.outcome: Distinguish safe action algebra from unsafe side-effect reordering. Proposed discriminator: In repetitive tool environments, explicit action/plan equivalence classes reduce fresh deliberation and adaptation cost under changing constraints while preserving verified effects.
